hypotheses.statement: For each of the fifteen R16 principles, the guarantee that matches it best by protected function is its ordinal counterpart, and no other guarantee is close
The functional match is exact for twelve principles and differs for P5, P10 and P15
Titles alone do not establish correspondence: some coincide and most differ in wording
P1 corresponds to no duty (G1 is named by no duty) and every duty is covered by at least one principle
The August Recursive Double Audit version is kept as a separate historical version

targets: a synthetic ledger, its worlds and the registries of duties, guarantees and governance principles

instrument_conditions.profiles: protected functions read from the supplied descriptions (this implementation's analytic reading, not verified against the sources); near pairs count 0.5

reproduction.world: xzr.teoo.lawledger on xzr.teoo.lawworld (own world and a world built to the stated R16 aggregates); registries in xzr.teoo.mheg

R901.criterion: the ordinal counterpart is the best and the only close guarantee for all fifteen
R901.reading: met on these profiles; the profiles are an analytic reading, so this shows what the supplied descriptions say, not what the sources say

near.reading: remedy is broader than material restoration
a challenge to the review mechanism overlaps a systemic challenge and a mutual audit

R902.criterion: exact for twelve; P5, P10, P15 differ

R903.criterion: some titles coincide and most differ

R904.criterion: only P1 has no duty; every duty has a principle

catalogue.source: The Minimum Guarantees of Human Legal Subjecthood, Publication Final V3.0, Chapter 6.2 (identical in the 100_POINT_EDITION and in R2 section 4: all fifteen titles and definitions compared character for character)
catalogue.note: V3.0 uses two vocabularies for the same five findings (Appendix A table: Secured/Partial/Absent/Indeterminate/Inapplicable; A.3 and 8.4 text: Satisfied/Partially Satisfied/Failed/Indeterminate/Not Applicable). R2 section 16 and this implementation use the table's.

note: results about a SYNTHETIC ledger; the stated-aggregates world is an independent verification model built to the stated numbers, not the manuscript's world, and its match is by construction; the principles' profiles are an analytic reading; a closure, a measurement or a match here is not a legal judgment or a restoration; not an observation of any institution, law or person
